steps.body: A tenths decimal and a tenths fraction name the same amount two ways: 0.7 and 7/10 are the same seven parts.
steps.narration: A tenths decimal and a tenths fraction name the same amount two ways: 0.7 and 7/10 are the same seven parts.

widget.prompt: Shade the strip to show 0.6. Each column is one tenth.

commonCounts.feedback: The count of shaded columns must match the tenths digit of 0.6 — that digit is 6, so 6 columns.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly 6 of the 10 columns — 6 tenths, which the decimal writes as 0.6.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Each column is one tenth — count the shaded columns against the decimal.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each column is one tenth — count the shaded columns against the decimal.

predict.prompt: You will shade 6 columns. Which fraction will name the same amount as the decimal 0.6?
predict.reveal: Six of ten equal parts is 6/10 — the fraction spells out what 0.6 abbreviates.

explanationVariants: The 7 sits in the tenths place, so the fraction is 7/10.

widget.prompt: Which fraction names the same amount as 0.7?

options.feedback: Correct — the digit 7 sits in the tenths place, so 0.7 means 7 of 10 equal parts.
A denominator of 100 would mean 7 hundredths, written 0.07. The digit 7 in 0.7 sits one place higher — in the tenths place.
That fraction has the part count and the number of equal pieces swapped. The decimal names 7 pieces out of 10 equal pieces, so 7 belongs on top.
A denominator of 1 would make this 7 whole units. The decimal point in 0.7 says the amount is less than one whole, cut into 10 equal parts.

widget.prompt: Write the fraction 3/10 as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: That drops the denominator. The fraction names 3 parts out of 10, so its decimal puts the 3 in the tenths place — a value less than one whole.
That writes 3 in the hundredths place, which names 3/100. Tenths sit one place higher: directly after the decimal point.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A denominator of 10 means tenths. Write the numerator in the tenths place, directly after the decimal point.
